title: A flat open neighbourhood of a quasi-compact generic-point subspace
statement: Let $C$ be a reduced quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Suppose the set $C_{\mathrm{gen}}$ of generic points of the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components], with the subspace Zariski topology, is quasi-compact. Let $h:Z\to C$ be of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], meaning locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. There exists a quasi-compact open subscheme $U\subseteq C$ containing $C_{\mathrm{gen}}$, dense in $C$, such that $h^{-1}(U)\to U$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. No Noetherianity or irreducibility assumption is made.

source.place: Lemma (3.5), printed p.12 (its proof chooses an open neighbourhood of all generic points before taking a quasi-compact subneighbourhood) Read online at the source URL; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Fix a component generic point $\eta\in C_{\mathrm{gen}}$ and choose an affine open $W_0=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq C$ containing it, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. If $K=\overline{\{\eta\}}$ is its component, then $K\cap W_0$ is a component of $W_0$: an irreducible subset containing it has irreducible closure in $C$ containing $K$, so maximality of $K$ forces that subset into $K\cap W_0$. Thus the prime $\mathfrak p$ corresponding to $\eta$ is minimal by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes]. The ring $R$ is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field], $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a field, and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies it with $\mathcal O_{C,\eta}$.

source.place: Tags 00ES (lemma-irreducible, part (3)) and 00EU (lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring); Schemes Tags 01IT and 01HV. Rydh (3.5), first sentence.

proof.text: For this $\eta$ and $W_0$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-spec-limit-affine-neighbourhoods] to the scheme $W_0$ and its point $\eta$. The inverse system consists of the affine opens $W\subseteq W_0$ containing $\eta$, ordered by reverse inclusion, with distinguished initial stage $W_0$. It is a nonempty directed set, the transitions are affine, the stages are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and its limit is $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{C,\eta}$ (restriction to an open does not change the stalk). Put $X_0=h^{-1}(W_0)$ and $f_0:X_0\to W_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), $f_0$ is of finite presentation; by (2), $X_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated since $W_0$ is. Its pullback to $S$ is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field], because step 1 makes $S$ the spectrum of a field. This verifies all finiteness and limit hypotheses needed for descent, without requiring $C$ to be irreducible or Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0GWT (lemma-morphism-glueing-near-closed-point), proof local-ring limit; Tag 01YW; Situation 081D. This expands Rydh (3.5) / EGA IV_3 Corollary 11.3.2 locally at a generic point.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-flat-finite-presentation] with base stages the $W$ of step 2, $S_0=Y_0=W_0$, $Y_i=W_i$, and $X_0=h^{-1}(W_0)$. The limit morphism is the flat morphism of step 2 and $f_0$ is locally of finite presentation. It follows that for some stage $W_\eta\subseteq W_0$ containing $\eta$, the base change $X_0\times_{W_0}W_\eta\to W_\eta$ is flat. This is exactly the restriction $h^{-1}(W_\eta)\to W_\eta$, since pulling back along an open inclusion takes the inverse-image open subscheme. In particular $W_\eta$ is an affine open of $C$.

The opens $W_\eta\cap C_{\mathrm{gen}}$ cover the subspace $C_{\mathrm{gen}}$. Its assumed quasi-compactness gives finitely many $\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_n$ whose opens cover it. Set $U=\bigcup_{j=1}^nW_{\eta_j}$. This is open and contains $C_{\mathrm{gen}}$. Each $W_{\eta_j}$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; hence $U$ is quasi-compact: restrict any open cover of $U$ to each of these finitely many opens, choose a finite subcover for each, and take their union. For any $z\in h^{-1}(U)$, choose $j$ with $h(z)\in W_{\eta_j}$. The local-ring map for the restriction to $U$ is the same as for the flat restriction to $W_{\eta_j}$, because stalks on open subspaces are the ambient stalks. Thus it is flat; [def-weil-flat-morphism] gives flatness of $h^{-1}(U)\to U$. If $C_{\mathrm{gen}}$ is empty, this construction uses the empty finite family and $U=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 01IT (affine open basis) and affine quasi-compactness; Rydh (3.5), second sentence; elementary finite-subcover and open-restriction stalk argument.

proof.text: For any $c\in C$, [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] supplies a component $K$ containing $c$, and [lem-sc-scheme-sober] supplies its generic point $\eta$. This point lies in $U$, and $c\in K=\overline{\{\eta\}}\subseteq\overline U$. Hence $\overline U=C$, proving density. In particular if $C_{\mathrm{gen}}=\varnothing$ then $C=\varnothing$, so the empty case in step 4 has all required properties.
